summary: The note reports on the 'Green Horizons Project', a set of eco-friendly infrastructure initiatives announced by Mayor Linda Harris in a district's neighborhoods. Projects include solar street lights, green spaces, tree planting, stormwater bio-retention, a greenway, a redesigned Lowell Bridge, rooftop solar, and IoT park sensors. Residents, educators, an economist and planners describe community, educational and economic benefits, and the note emphasizes how the effort is building stronger community bonds.
one_line: Mayor Linda Harris launched the Green Horizons Project in 2023, bringing solar power, green spaces, a greened Lowell Bridge and smart tech to local neighborhoods.
key_facts: Mayor Linda Harris unveiled the 'Green Horizons Project' on Tuesday, September 5, 2023, at Jefferson Park.
Announced projects include solar-powered street lights, urban green spaces, extensive tree planting campaigns, and bio-retention systems to manage stormwater runoff.
Emily Nguyen, a long-time resident and mother of two, is excited about new playgrounds with recycled rubber surfaces and native plant landscaping.
Carlos Mendez's café, popular for its organic blends, sits adjacent to the proposed greenway, a corridor for pedestrians and bicyclists.

A partnership with local schools created 'Green Classrooms', where students take part in learning and conservation activities; Jefferson High teacher Michael Johnson says it bridges the gap between theory and reality.
The aging Lowell Bridge over the Clearwater River began redesign work in late October 2023, using renewable construction materials and hanging gardens beneath its span.
Project engineer Avery Robertson described the bridge work as 'rehabilitating a community symbol'.
Some residents initially worried about tax hikes and higher costs of living, but job creation and potential property value gains have shifted perspectives.
Economist Dr. Jasmine Patel spoke at a town hall meeting on November 15, 2023, saying the projects are investments that will lead to job diversity, especially in the green sector.
The Suburban Solar Initiative (SSI) aims to install rooftop solar panels with a focus on public buildings and schools, and facilitates group buys of solar panels for homeowners.
Engineer David Kim, an advocate for renewable energy, already has panels installed on his rooftop.
IoT sensors in parks monitor plant health and soil moisture, telling maintenance crews when to water and tend greenery.
City planner Lisa Wright presented on the smart technologies on December 1, 2023, at the community center, saying they enhance rather than replace nature.
Residents are coming together in workshops, visioning sessions and volunteer activities; landscape architect Tina Gomez says these efforts deepen relationships with the environment and each other.
